claim: AAAI 2025's counterexample-guided repair paper combines formal-methods (MaxSAT) fault localization with zero-shot LLM synthesis in a CEGIS loop, evaluated on 1,431 real incorrect student programs across six different LLMs.
stance_target: scale/breadth of evaluation expected at AAAI for a code-LLM + localization contribution
scope_conditions: introductory programming assignments (IPAs), six evaluated LLMs
quoted_support: Experiments on 1,431 incorrect student programs show that the counterexample guided approach, using MaxSAT-based bug-free program sketches, significantly improves the repair capabilities of all six evaluated LLMs.

claim: The paper explicitly frames its contribution as combining complementary strengths: formal-methods fault localization excels at identifying buggy parts of a program, while LLMs excel at completing strings/synthesizing fixes.
stance_target: framing pattern rewarded at AAAI: hybrid symbolic + neural methods with a clear complementarity argument
quoted_support: LLMs excel at completing strings, while FM-based fault localization excel at identifying buggy parts of a program. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines the strengths of both FM-based fault localization and LLMs, via zero-shot learning, to enhance APR for IPAs.

claim: The counterexample-guided approach outperforms both pure-LLM repair and state-of-the-art symbolic program repair tools, and produces smaller (less invasive) fixes, not just more repairs.
stance_target: value of pairing localization signal with generation for both quantity and quality (minimality) of fixes
quoted_support: This method allows LLMs to repair more programs with smaller fixes, outperforming other configurations and state-of-the-art symbolic program repair tools.

claim: Existing FM-based semantic repair tools can only fix programs when the correct implementation shares the same control-flow graph as the buggy one, a structural limitation that motivates combining them with LLMs.
stance_target: known limitation of pure formal-methods program repair used to justify hybrid approach
quoted_support: These tools excel at identifying buggy parts but can only fix programs if the correct implementation and the faulty one share the same control flow graph.
